question: A 3-year-old boy presents with his mother to the family medicine clinic for an itchy rash on the face that started 3 days ago. The mother states that her son had a fever with a runny nose a little more than a week ago. There has been no sore throat or cough according to the mother. No significant medical conditions are noted. No medications are on record. The boy is up-to-date on all immunizations. His heart rate is 102/min, respiratory rate is 24/min, temperature is 36.5°C (101.6°F), and blood pressure is 92/65 mm Hg. The boy appears well-nourished and alert. Auscultation of the heart is without murmurs. Lungs are clear to auscultation bilaterally. An erythematous malar rash extending from the left lateral nasal region to the left medial zygomatic region is present. There is no lymphadenopathy present. A full skin examination reveals an erythematous, reticulated rash on the lower extremities (see image). Which of the following etiologic agents is responsible for the patient’s signs and symptoms?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: Fever with runny nose a little more than a week ago -> Itchy rash on the face starting 3 days ago -> Erythematous malar rash extending from left lateral nasal to left medial zygomatic region -> Erythematous, reticulated rash on lower extremities -> Parvovirus B19 -> 95%

CHAIN: Fever with runny nose a little more than a week ago -> Itchy rash on the face starting 3 days ago -> Erythematous malar rash extending from left lateral nasal to left medial zygomatic region -> Erythematous, reticulated rash on lower extremities -> Human herpesvirus 6 (HHV-6) -> 85%
enhanced_information: The patient's presentation of fever with runny nose followed by an itchy rash on the face, extending to the lower extremities, is most likely due to Parvovirus B19 based on the erythematous malar rash and reticulated rash on the lower extremities. The evidence paths support this by indicating the association of Parvovirus B19 with exanthema and its presence in the lower extremities. Human herpesvirus 6 is less likely in this case.
analysis: The patient's presentation of fever with runny nose followed by an itchy rash on the face, extending to the lower extremities, along with the erythematous malar rash and reticulated rash on the lower extremities, is highly suggestive of Parvovirus B19 infection. Parvovirus B19 is known to cause a characteristic 'slapped cheek' rash on the face and a lace-like rash on the extremities. The absence of lymphadenopathy and the specific rash pattern seen in this case further support this diagnosis.
